descriptor.can_do: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) of main lexical verbs with auxiliary 'do'.
examples: Do you remember Julie? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)
Did you buy a new mobile phone? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can form questions with a 'wh-' word as subject, without an auxiliary verb.
examples: What happened? (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD)
Who cares? (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD)
Who knows? (Portuguese, B1 THRESHOLD)

descriptor.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.
examples: My favourite song is 'Viva la vida'. Do you know it? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)
My bedroom will be blue!! I love this colour!! Do you like it? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)
Yesterday, I went to buy some new clothes at the new store that is opposite my house, do you remember it? (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
Did you see the football match last night? (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Marathi; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + main verb 'be' + subject to form 'wh-' questions.
examples: How was your dinner yesterday? (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
How are you, my friend? (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Hindi; Pass)
Where are you, men? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Portuguese; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the auxiliary verb 'do' in an affirmative declarative clause, for emphasis and affirmation.
examples: Yes, I do have a favorite restaurant. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
I do miss you. (Syria; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Arabic - Levant; Pass)
I do apologise for the change but I can't be there on the 28th of June. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Italian; Pass)
After all, you did say that you wanted go somewhere with your friends. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can form interrogative clauses ('yes/no' forms) with auxiliary 'be' and 'have'.
examples: Are you going to the new art class? (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Turkish; Pass)
Have you got a new dress for the party? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'be' + subject + the '-ing' form (continuous form) to form 'yes/no' questions.
examples: Are you going to come? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Catalan; Pass)
Are you feeling better? (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
Are you going to the new art class? (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Turkish; Pass)
Are you doing anything on Friday? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Chinese; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can form interrogative clauses with 'be'.
examples: How are you? (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Farsi; Pass)
Are you ok? (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Thai; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verb 'be', with contracted and uncontracted forms.
examples: My college is not very big. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)
I know you are not well. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; French; Pass)
I'm not a good swimmer. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Romanian; Pass)
This place isn't big. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Lithuanian; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use 'yes/no', 'wh-', tag and negative question forms with an increasing range of verbs.
examples: Are you still looking for a job or did you succeed in finding one? (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)
When did you last see your wife and your children? (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; German; Pass)
It was great to have met you, and we certainly had a terrific time together, didn't we? (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)
Didn't you tell me that you had to go to Orleans today? (B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)
Why didn't you say something about it? (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

retained_mapping.note: Inseparable mixed supported and unsupported construction: question forms include out-of-scope question tags.

descriptor.can_do: Can use 'shall' with 'we' to make suggestions.
examples: Tomorrow evening there is Laura Pausini's concert in Turin. Shall we go? (Italian, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)
Shall we go to a Korean restaurant after the film? (Korean, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2003)

retained_mapping.note: phase2 contradiction: clause=declarative; evidence: examples use interrogative 'Shall we ...?' forms.

descriptor.can_do: Can use a limited range of question tags.
examples: You don't know where I live, do you? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)
It differs from the story which you told me, doesn't it? (Japan; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Japanese; Pass)
It's fantastic, isn't it? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Italian; Pass)
It cost £30, it was not too expensive, was it? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

retained_mapping.note: Question tags are a declared unsupported construction.

descriptor.guideword: FORM/USE: REAL AND IMAGINED SITUATIONS AFTER 'IF'
descriptor.can_do: Can use the present simple after 'if' to talk about real and imagined situations.
examples: If you want some help, I will be free next week. (Key English Test, A2, French)
If you go with your parents, you will go walking or swimming, but if you go with friends, you will have more fun. (Key English Test, A2, German)
Don't forget to wear colourful clothes because if you wear white clothes, you will get paint on them. (Key English Test, A2, Thai)
[talking about a toothbrush] It is very important for me because if I don't have it, I can't clean my teeth. (Key English Test, A2, Thai)

retained_mapping.note: Linked conditional construction is out of scope.

descriptor.can_do: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb with 'not only … but' as a focusing device. ► focus ► inversion
examples: Not only have I been wandering its streets ever since I was ten, but I have also come to know most of the main characters of its history in the past 50 years. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Catalan; Pass)

Not only have I been expecting it for the last few months but I will also give some support to my wife, who has been feeling a little nervous these last weeks. (Portugal; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

retained_mapping.note: The 'not only … but' focusing construction is a multi-clause relational construction not representable as one GrammarCell.

descriptor.can_do: Can use the passive infinitive after a limited number of forms including 'going to', 'have to', 'need to', 'want to'.
examples: It is going to be shown this Friday. (B1 PET Turkish)
After that, they printed an authorisation, form which had to be signed by my parents because I'm not over eighteen. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)
He wants to be informed about sales development by the end of November 2001. (B1 Switzerland German)

retained_mapping.note: Passive infinitives governed by forms including the deferred periphrastic modals 'be going to' and 'have to' are outside the single-clause ontology.

descriptor.can_do: Can form interrogative clauses with an adverb in mid position, between the subject and the main verb.
examples: Have you ever been to Marseille? (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; French; Pass)
What kind of books do you usually read? (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Italian; Pass)
Do you still remember my best friend? (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

retained_mapping.note: Adverb placement within interrogative clauses is non-verbal grammar and is not represented by the schema.

descriptor.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of regular and irregular verbs.
examples: They are very important to me, because they bring me good luck. (Key English Test, A2,Bulgarian)
I hope you can come next time. (Key English Test, A2,Portuguese)
The journey takes about half an hour from Paris. (Key English Test, A2, French)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
examples: The player from China did not look very happy though. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Chinese; Pass)
You did not keep your promise. (Bangladesh; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Bengali; Pass)
I didn't tell you that my house is opposite the new cinema. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)
They didn't cost much ... (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Panjabi; Pass)
I was surprised because the heating didn't work. (Poland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Polish; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the negative form.
examples: [talking about a computer] I’m not using it any more. (A2 Turkish)
…the fridge isn't working. (Romanian, ===NONE===, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2009)
… he's going to work at 5.00 am, so he's not eating anything ... (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Polish; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the negative form 'haven't' + '-ed' with 'I' with a limited range of verbs.
examples: I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time. (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
I haven't seen you for a long time. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Hungarian; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the question form.
examples: Was my mother going to die? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)
I couldnt see anybody, then there he was, my hero, my favorite singer Bob Dylan saying my name, but was he calling me? (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)
What were you doing? (Uzbekhistan (Republic of); B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Russian; Pass)
[talking about a dream] Everything was strange. Why was I following a green fox? (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use question forms.
examples: Had I made the same mistake twice? (B2; 1993; German; Pass)
… the question was: Why had he done that? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the passive with modal verbs in a range of contexts, with a variety of subjects.
examples: Architects should be hired to design parks, where people could go for a walk or have a picnic. (B2 Polish)
Although I had a marvellous time, I believe there are a few things that could be improved for next year's festival. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Greek; Pass)
As a result, today, it could be said that nearly everyone is living in a digital world which means computers are necessary and very important. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

descriptor.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple affirmative and negative forms with modal verbs to refer to the past.
examples: I think that all these problems could have been avoided and that asking for my money back is the best way of forgetting that evening. (B2 Catalan)
I don't remember how I lost it, it might have been stolen. (B2 Japanese)
Of course, some groups were better than others but I think they all played well and have talent: they should have been given a chance! (B2 Italian)
It should not have been used in this kind of article. (B2 Korean)
